Hi Sarah —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap + proposed POC plan so we have clear next steps. I captured this after our call; please flag anything off.

High-level objective:
- Validate Redwood inference for FinSight’s "Smart Insights" feature: low-latency summaries + entity extraction with tool-calling to your internal knowledge graph.

Proposed POC (4 weeks):
1) Week 0 (kickoff): access + test account, baseline metrics collection (current latency/cost).
2) Week 1: Integrate SDK (Python/Node) and wire /v1/generate for batch summarization; run smoke tests.
3) Week 2: Streamed narratives for interactive UI (SSE) + enable function/tool calling for KG lookups.
4) Week 3: Run evaluation prompts (10k tokens worth) against success criteria; iterate quant/ batching.
5) Week 4: Final report + recommendation (rollout vs. next steps).

Proposed success criteria (suggested; update if you prefer):
- Latency: 95th %ile < 300ms for 1–2k token responses in interactive flow.
- Quality: precision/recall on entity extraction >= 90% on agreed evaluation set.
- Cost: average token cost per request < $0.02 (goal).
- Integration: stable streaming with reconnect/resumption and function call reliability at 99% success.

Ownership & contacts:
- FinSight: Sarah (EM), Alex Chen (Lead Engineer) — you to provide sample prompts, eval dataset, and a test environment.
- Redwood: Vivek (SE lead) — integration/ops; Marissa (commercial) — POC coordination; Karthik — SDK/infra support.

Attachments: I attached a short success criteria doc and a POC implementation map (spreadsheet) with proposed milestones.

Next steps I propose now:
- You confirm the success criteria and Alex as the primary technical contact.
- Schedule a 30-min kickoff next Tue/Thu — Vivek will walk the integration steps.
- Provide API access details or a dev sandbox by EOD Friday so we can start Week 1 tasks.

Thanks — excited to get this running.

Hi Sarah / Alex —

Thanks for the notes — below is a concise integration plan answering your technical questions and confirming tradeoffs. Happy to expand into a spin-up checklist in the attached PDF.

1) Latency target 
- 250ms 95th is aggressive but achievable for short responses (<=512 tokens) if we enable prefix/KV caching and run the model on a dedicated inference lane (low-concurrency, quantized model variant). Expect slightly higher times for long (>1k tokens) responses. We’ll instrument and baseline in Week 0.

2) SDKs & Streaming
- Node (TypeScript) SDK: fully supported. We use chunked SSE for streaming in the SDK with automatic reconnect and resume token support. That will work with EventSource, but for reliable resume we recommend a small client-side buffer that accepts chunk ids from the server.
- Python SDK: recommended for batch evaluation jobs; it supports direct async streaming and efficient token batching.

3) API routes (examples)
- POST /v1/generate -> non-stream batch generation (JSON request/response).
- POST /v1/stream -> SSE endpoint for interactive streaming. Returns chunk metadata (chunk_id, token_index) to support resume.
- POST /v1/tool_call -> function-calling handshake: model returns a call syntax; client confirms execution and POSTs the results to /v1/tool_call/complete.

4) Function/tool calling & reliability pattern
- Idempotency: include a call_id (UUID) on each tool invocation. Redwood will only forward unique call_id once to the tool endpoint.
- Rate limits: default 200 calls/min per tenant; we can adjust for the POC if necessary.
- Retries/backoff: client should implement exponential backoff with jitter (initial 200ms, max 5s) and allow 3 attempts for transient 5xx errors. For long-running KG queries, prefer async callback (we support callback URLs).

5) Caching & batching knobs for cost vs latency
- Prefix caching for repeated prompts (esp. templates) — reduces repeated token decode and improves latency.
- Dynamic batching: we can set a max latency budget (e.g., 15ms batch wait) — tradeoff is slightly increased p50 but much better throughput. We'll provide recommended presets based on your expected qps.

6) POC timeline (revised)
- Thu Mar 05 (Kickoff): Vivek + Alex deep-dive; share access and keys.
- Week 1: SDK integration + /v1/generate batch tests (owner: Alex, support: Karthik).
- Week 2: Streaming integration + tool-calling handshake; run smoke for reconnection (owner: Alex & FinSight frontend).
- Week 3: Run evals (FinSight provides datasets); measure success criteria; iterate caching/quantization.
- Week 4: Final report + operational checklist and recommendation.

7) Owners and escalation
- FinSight: Alex Chen (engineering) — provide datasets, sandbox, and test users.
- Redwood SE: Vivek Kulkarni — technical lead.
- Commercial: Marissa Cole — contract/SOW and procurement triage.
- CS: Monica Patel — post-POC onboarding and onboarding plan if POC succeeds.

8) Deliverables
- Week-by-week test log, perf dashboards (access to Redwood Console), and a final POC report with cost/latency projection for production.

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (detailed spin-up tasks) and POC-implementation-map.xlsx (milestones).

If that all looks good, we’ll proceed with Thu 11am PT kickoff. I can send a calendar invite once Sarah confirms.

Cheers,
